figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Thioesters, seco-acids, macrolactones, and their precursors. (A) (1) 10-deoxymethynolide (10-DML) and (2) narbonolide, the 12- and
14-membered macrolactones that serve as precursors for all substrates. (B) Comparison of (4) 6-deoxyerythronolide B and (7) tylactone with
positions 3−5 and adjacent functional groups highlighted in blue. (C) Hypothetical conversion of SNAC hexaketide (10a) to seco-acid (10b) and
macrolactone (10c). (D) Hypothetical conversion of SNAC heptaketide (11a) to seco-acid (11b) and macrolactone (11c). (E) Hypothetical
conversion of SNAC heptaketide (12a) to seco-acid (12b) and macrolactone (12c).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Organization and composition of the T1ALPKS TE library. Each color represents a discrete TE group defined by phylogenetic and
biosynthetic gene cluster analysis: GreenGroup 1,2 10-DML/narbonolide synthases; AquaGroup 3 8,8a-deoxyoleandolide synthase(s);
BlueGroup 4 6-deoxyerythronolide B synthases; PurpleGroup 5 8,15-dideoxylankanolide synthases; PinkGroup 6 platenolide I synthases;
CoralGroup 7 tylactone synthases; OrangeGroup 8 chalcolactone synthase(s); YellowGroup 9 protomycinolide IV synthase(s). TEs that
contain an “H” in their names are homologues of a reference TE (reference TEs are derived from known producers of a macrolactone with well-
defined T1ALPKSs). TEs that contain an asterisk in their names are active site Ser→Cys mutants. Bootstrap values for this tree and an expanded
phylogenetic tree of type I TEs are presented in Section S5.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Reactions of wild-type T1ALPKS TEs with substrates (A) (10a), (B) (11a), and (C) (12a). Each graph displays the yields of
macrolactones (10c), (11c), or (12c), the yields of seco-acids (10b), (11b), or (12b), and the % recovery of the starting thioesters (10a), (11a), or
(12a). Control reactions contain no enzyme. Each data point represents the average values obtained from two reactions. Colored bars and group
labels (G1−G9) denote TE group classification. See Section S9.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Reactions of Ser→Cys T1ALPKS TEs with substrates (A) (10a), (B) (11a), and (C) (12a). Each graph displays the yields of
macrolactones (10c), (11c), or (12c), the yields of seco-acids (10b), (11b), or (12b), and the % recovery of the starting thioesters (10a), (11a),
(12a). Control reactions contain no enzyme. Each data point represents the average values obtained from two reactions. All Ser→Cys mutants are
denoted with an asterisk (*). Black boxes contain wild-type and mutant thioesterase pairs. See Section S9.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Kinetic Resolutions with Thioesterases. (A) Ring-forming kinetic resolution of a mixture of thioesters (12a) and (11a). (B) Ring-opening
kinetic resolution of a mixture of macrolactones (12c) and (11c). Yields were calculated based on the quantities of each diastereomer of starting
material, not the sum of the diastereomeric starting materials.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Prep-scale reactions with thioesterases. Ring-forming prep-scale reactions were conducted with thioesters (10a), (11a), and (12a). Ring-
opening prep-scale reaction with macrolactone (12c).
